Date: Mon, 09 Jul 2028 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Contract redline: runtime execution access — request Product/Security consensus

Team —

Legal received a redline from MedBase (attached) that adds a new paragraph giving them the right to request "runtime execution access" for debugging and export purposes. High level: they want the ability to have Redwood run short-lived queries against customer-specific runtime traces and telemetry, and to request limited extraction of logs/outputs for compliance review.

Key asks from Legal: we need Product + Security sign-off on whether the requested access is acceptable as-written, and if not, propose replacement language. Specific questions to answer:
- Is the proposed retention window reasonable? (they propose 90 days)
- Does the scope (full model outputs vs. metadata only) make sense operationally and legally?
- Any product changes required to support an "export on request" workflow?

I attached MedBase_runtime_access_redline_v1.docx — Olga has the detailed markup. Can Product and Security please review and provide proposed language or explicit objections by EOD Wednesday (2028-07-11)? Dev, please confirm whether this would block the current implementation timeline for the pilot.

Thanks — I want to move quickly because Procurement is waiting.

Sean
Sean Gallagher
Director, Sales Ops | Redwood Inference
sean@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Contract redline: runtime execution access — request Product/Security consensus

Sean / all —

Thanks for flagging this. I reviewed the vendor redline and produced a tracked-change version with two alternatives: (A) a narrow, auditable access clause limited to "metadata and invocation traces necessary to reproduce a specific incident" and (B) a broader clause that includes "model outputs" but only where explicitly scoped and customer-authorized.

Open items from Legal's perspective:
- We should not accept a standing right to export full model outputs without a clear security AND product mitigation plan.
- Retention: 90 days as-proposed is high. Legal prefers 30 days unless Product/Security provide rationale for longer.
- Subprocessors: the clause must require Redwood to publish the subprocessor list and give the customer a review period for any new subprocessor that would touch exported artifacts.

I've attached MedBase_runtime_access_redline_v1.docx with inline comments and a short summary. Suggest we converge on a single counterproposal to present back.

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Hi —

Product viewpoint below based on engineering feasibility and customer impact. TL;DR: we can support a narrow, auditable export workflow; the broader "full output" export will materially increase risk and operational cost.

Concerns and proposed language:
- KV cache / prefix retention: we cannot expose cached prefixes or unredacted user inputs. Proposed: exports limited to request-level metadata, timestamps, and anonymized token-level metrics. No raw customer prompt text or KV cache snapshots unless explicit written approval and a validated Data Use Request.
- Retention: 30 days is reasonable for telemetry; 7 days preferred for debug traces that include non-sensitive inputs. If customer needs 90 days for compliance, we offer a separate paid "audit export" that runs in a secure enclave with customer-provided KMS and explicit data-handling SOPs.
- Operational impact: to implement any "on-request" extraction we need a short spec and a one-week demo run for the pilot — this will add ~2 sprint tasks to infra backlog. Dev, please confirm the timeline.

Suggested clause (summary): "Redwood will provide limited, auditable access to execution metadata and anonymized traces for a bounded retention period (default 30 days). Full output extracts are permitted only with customer-approved scope, reviewed subprocessor list, and use of an encrypted export pipeline under customer KMS."

I can draft the exact contract language once Security confirms encryption/KMS requirements.

Thanks —
Irene Choi
Group Product Manager, Runtime

Subject: Re: Contract redline: runtime execution access — request Product/Security consensus

Security / Privacy notes: I agree with narrowing scope. A few controls we must insist on in the clause or via an Exhibit:
- Encryption: exports and logs must be encrypted at rest and in transit using customer-specific KMS keys when requested by the customer.
- Access control: only named roles (SRE/security) may approve and perform exports; access must be logged to the audit trail with justification.
- Subprocessor transparency: require a 30-day review period for any new subprocessor that would touch exported artifacts.
- Data minimization: default export must redact PII and sensitive fields; if MedBase requests raw outputs, they must provide a legal justification and sign a separate DUA.

I've updated the security-checklist_runtime_access.xlsx and attached it. I also added a suggested clause to the redline that maps to our SOC 2 controls and KMS integration. If Product can accept the "secure enclave export" option for longer retention we can close this without engineering changing core runtime behavior.

Marissa Cole
Security & Privacy Lead

Anna / MedBase team —

Thanks for patience while we looped in Product and Security. Below is the consolidated Redwood counterproposal and next steps. Please review and confirm whether this meets MedBase's audit needs or if you want us to schedule a short call to walk through the export controls.

Redwood summary of agreed constraints (to be formalized in the redline):
- Scope: Exports limited to execution metadata and anonymized traces by default. Full model output extracts are allowed only when explicitly requested in writing and scoped in an Exhibit.
- Retention: Default telemetry retention 30 days. Debug traces that include sensitive inputs will have a 7-day default retention. Extended retention (e.g., 90 days) can be provided via a secure enclave export under customer KMS with an agreed SOP and separate fee.
- Security controls: All exports encrypted in transit and at rest. Customer may request use of customer-managed KMS for exports. Access requires named role approval and is logged for audit.
- Subprocessors: Redwood will publish an up-to-date subprocessor list and give MedBase 30-day notice for any subprocessor changes that impact export handling.

Attachments: merged redline (MedBase_runtime_access_redline_v1.docx) and security checklist. Drive link with detailed redline: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redlines
DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/transaction/XYZ-12345

Next steps we propose:
1) MedBase to confirm whether the secure-enclave + KMS option satisfies the 90-day retention requirement. If yes, we mark Exhibit A for the audit export and move to signature.
2) If MedBase insists on default 90-day retention for all traces, we need to scope potential product changes and revised pricing — this will push the pilot by ~4 weeks.
3) If confirmed, Legal will provide final redline by EOD Monday and Procurement can route for signature.

If you prefer a quick sync, we can set up a 30-min call Monday.

Thanks —
Sean
Director, Sales Ops | Redwood Inference
sean@redwood.com
